rationale: Option A includes a control from an untrained teacher on identical text, which is a cheap, clear way to detect real transfer, and shared initialization is the standard condition for subliminal learning. Option B's attention-only LoRA plus a second sampled-token student adds cost and complexity, and there is no control for the text itself. A pragmatic, resource-conscious evaluator would lean slightly toward A, but B's comparison and cheaper LoRA training keep it plausible.
